newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FORECAST - Ommeren '96 net seen up 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Ommeren '96 net seen up 15 pct.

text.p: Dutch shipping and tank storage firm Koninklijke van Ommeren is expected to realise its forecast of a "clearly higher" 1996 net profit when it reports on Thursday, analysts said.
However, net profit excluding extraordinary items will be only marginally higher, despite improvements in Van Ommeren's shipping and chemical tank storage activities.

Analysts predict a tight range of net profit from 91 million to 96 million guilders, a rise of about 15 percent on the 1995 figure of 80.3 million guilders which included an extraordinary charge of 11.4 million guilders.

In tank shipping, the company is expected to have benefited from new vessels and some improvement in freight rates, which slumped in 1995. However, this year's results will not be propped up by book profits from the sale of ships.
"We see a higher contribution from tanker shipping, although it's perhaps more to do with the expansion of (Van Ommeren's) fleet," says Andre Mulder of BZW.
The company added five ships in 1996. Three more are expected to be completed in 1997 and one more next year.

In tank storage, the company is at an advantage compared with rivals because it has a high proportion of long term contracts, which have insulated it from volatile product prices. Its chemical storage activities have performed particularly well, analysts said.
"Volumes in the second half in tank storage were better. Chemical margins were undoubtedly the highest (of its storage activities)," said Pieter van Gelder of Delta Lloyd Bank.
Analysts are generally maintaining a hold recommendation, with some modest earnings growth expected in the coming years.
"Further improvements in tank storage can be expected and some in ocean tankers, but we're keeping Van Ommeren on a rating of market performer for now," said Gert Jochems of NIB Strating.
